newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO to appeal bond case judgement.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO to appeal bond case judgement.

text.p: ABN AMRO said on Thursday it would appeal an Amsterdam court ruling holding the Dutch bank liable for damages to investors in a bond issue, for German retail concern Co op, which it lead managed in 1987 and 1988.
The court ruled on August 28 in favour of a group of Co op bond holders who claimed to have been misled by the prospectus for the issue after Co op collapsed in October 1988.
"Because this concerns a fundamental principle for the new-issue business, ABN AMRO is appealing the judgement of the court," the bank said in a statement.

"The court is comparing the conduct of ABN AMRO in this affair against norms which, according to the bank, are stricter than those which are applied legally in surrounding countries," the statement said.

"This threatens to create a situation in which the new-issue business of the banks in the Netherlands will diverge from international practices, which could hinder the business activities of banks here."
The court ruled that ABN AMRO was responsible for the contents of the Co op prospectus, which assured investors of the group's financial health.

Some investors who sold their bonds after Co op's problems emerged lost money as the bonds plunged to less than 60 percent of their face value, but most retained them and were paid in full by Asko AG, which bought much of Co op's business.
The 80 investors who brought the suit bought some 200 million guilders worth of the issue. The size of damages sought is not yet known. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
